advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Surface (or assert non-empty against expectation) the `skipped` criteria from ProductionBatchRunner in full mode rather than letting unknown ids vanish silently.
evidence:
production_batch_runner.py:236-243: `desc = by_id.get(cid)
        if desc is None:
            skipped.append(cid)
            logger.warning(... is not in the criteria registry; skipping)`
tier2.py:668-674 (single mode) DOES raise on unknown id: `if desc is None: raise ValueError(f"tier2: unknown criterion id ...")`
full_mode_request_criteria (tier2.py:310-329) builds the tuple from route_criteria and never surfaces which requested ids ProductionBatchRunner later drops into `skipped`
advisory.finding: full_mode_request_criteria / run_candidate_pass1 rely on _resolve_criteria's silent skip path for ids absent from the live registry: an unknown/renamed id is logged and dropped, never raised. Single-criterion mode explicitly fails fast on an unknown id, but full mode has no equivalent guard, so a candidate overlay that renames or removes a criterion silently under-requests without any signal in the run result.
scenarios: A candidate .rebar overlay that renames criterion ids: full mode silently reviews fewer criteria and the Jaccard/flip numbers look plausible but measure a smaller criteria set

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a finding-set-comparison test with a SINGLE stored finding tagged mixed criteria (e.g. ['P6','E1']) asserting it is NOT excluded by _exclude_det_findings.
evidence: tier2.py `_exclude_det_findings`: return [f for f in findings if not (f.get("criteria") and set(f["criteria"]) <= _DET_CRITERIA)]
docstring: "Drop stored findings whose criteria are ENTIRELY DET-floor tier"

test_plan_replay_tier2.py:281 test_finding_set_comparison_keeps_non_det_stored_finding_alongside_det uses two SEPARATE findings [_finding(...,["P6"]), _finding(...,["E1"])], not one finding tagged ["P6","E1"]
ABSENCE: no test constructs a single finding with mixed DET+non-DET criteria to assert it is KEPT
advisory.finding: `_exclude_det_findings`'s subset semantics for a MIXED-criteria single finding are untested. The added line `not (f.get('criteria') and set(f['criteria']) <= _DET_CRITERIA)` keeps a finding tagged with BOTH a DET-floor and a non-DET criterion, but no test drives a single finding with `criteria=['P6','E1']`; existing tests only use single-criterion or two separate findings, so the subset check never sees a multi-element set. A regression using intersection instead of subset (dropping any finding touching a DET criterion) would pass all current tests.
scenarios: A candidate/stored finding tagged with a DET criterion plus a real Pass-1 criterion (e.g. ['P6','E1']) is incorrectly excluded if the subset check is weakened to intersection
advisory.suggested_fix: Add: stored = [_finding('wombat platypus koala echidna', ['P6','E1'])]; assert tier2.finding_set_comparison(stored, [])['per_criterion'] == {'P6': {...lost:1}, 'E1': {...lost:1}} (finding retained because its criteria set is not a subset of CANONICAL_DET).

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a test that forces `git worktree remove` to fail (e.g. monkeypatch subprocess.run to return non-zero for the remove) and asserts the rmtree+prune fallback runs.
evidence: tier2.py cleanup_reconstructed_ticket: if result.returncode != 0: shutil.rmtree(scratch_root, ignore_errors=True); subprocess.run(["git","worktree","prune"...])
ABSENCE: grep of test file shows cleanup_reconstructed_ticket only called at lines 164/192/230 as teardown, never with a forced non-zero worktree-remove
advisory.finding: `cleanup_reconstructed_ticket`'s failure-recovery branch (git worktree remove returncode != 0 -> shutil.rmtree + `git worktree prune`) is never exercised; the function is only invoked on the happy path as teardown in other tests.
scenarios: A `git worktree remove` failure (dirty scratch worktree, missing registration) should fall back to rmtree+prune; a regression removing that fallback leaks worktree registrations

blocking.checklist_item: - [ ] Fix candidate_verdict_flip so an empty candidate still reports the stored blocking criteria as relieved (do not zero stored_blocking_criteria on the empty-candidate short-circuit).
evidence: tier2.py:463-464: `if not candidate_findings:\n        return {"stored_blocking_criteria": set(), "candidate_blocking_criteria": set()}`
tier2.py:500-507 verdict_flip_matrix: `stored = flip["stored_blocking_criteria"] ... relieved += len(stored - candidate)` — with stored forced empty, relieved contributes 0 for empty-candidate rows

The commit message itself notes the empty-finding-set degenerate signature was the exact bug being chased (relieved~19-20/20); an early-return that zeroes stored blocking on empty candidate would UNDERreport relieved for exactly those rows, the opposite direction, but still a measurement distortion masking the empty-candidate case
blocking.finding: candidate_verdict_flip returns stored_blocking_criteria=set() whenever candidate_findings is empty, discarding the row's real stored blocking criteria. verdict_flip_matrix then computes relieved += len(stored - candidate) = 0 for that row, so an empty candidate finding set (the degenerate failure signature) reports zero 'relieved' instead of the maximum. The flip metric cannot distinguish 'candidate matched the stored verdict' from 'candidate produced nothing'.
scenarios: A candidate whose Pass-1 emits nothing for a review whose stored verdict blocked on some criterion — the flip matrix records that row as neither newly_blocking nor relieved, hiding a total loss of coverage
blocking.suggested_fix: On the empty-candidate branch, return the real stored_blocking (computed via _exclude_det_findings) with candidate_blocking_criteria=set(), rather than an empty stored set.

evidence: tier2.py:614-618: each row calls candidate_verdict_flip(..., run_chunk=verify_run_chunk, ...) which issues verify_findings -> verify_run_chunk billable calls beyond run_candidate_pass1
ledger.py:35 PER_SAMPLE_ESTIMATE_USD tier2:3.4 is a single flat per-sample rate not obviously accounting for the added verify pass
dropped.finding: run_tier2_full reserves budget with only ledger.estimate(_TIER, len(sample)) but each row also makes billable Pass-2 verifier calls via verify_run_chunk (in addition to the Pass-1 batch run). The pre-flight reserve therefore under-estimates true spend; finalize prices all usage rows correctly, but the reserve gate can admit a run that ultimately costs more than the reserved estimate.
scenarios: A near-cap run where the extra verifier spend per row pushes cumulative spend past the intended reserve headroom
